MARANON Province of Negros Occidental Dear Governor Marafion: DILG Opinion No. 3, s. 2013 24 JAN 2013 This has reference to your letter dated 03 January 2013 re uesting this Department's opinion regarding your 2013 Annual Budget which was disappro ed in its entirety by your sanggunian by a vote of 9-5 without them stating the reas ns or grounds for their disapproval. Specifically, you want to be clarified on the following issues, to wit: "1. Can our Sanggunian disapprove in its entirety ou Annual Budget without stating the reasons or grounds for their disappro al? 2. Can I veto the disapproval of our entire Annual Bud et? 3. If I can veto the disapproval, what is the effect i the Sanggunian cannot override my veto? 4. If we operate on a re-enacted budget, can we utilize the following: 20% Provincial Development Fund for the pay ent of our loans a. which are also our contractual obligations? b. c. d. 20% Provincial Development Fund for the impl mentation of our continuing projects like the operation of our arms? These said Farms are occupied and without the budget to nd the operation animals will perish. Grants and Donations account under the Offic of the Governor ,which is part our previous year's Annual Budget Gender and Development projects which is nder our Special Purpose Appropriations? 5. Can the Sanggunian take up in their session other atters even if we don't have yet an approved Annual Budget in view o Sec. 323 of the Local Government Code?" As to the first question, we answer in the negative. Let it be noted that the annual budget, properly referred to as an executive budget 7160)1 refers to a budget under Section 318 of the Local Government Code of 1991 ( 1 Section 318. Prepa-ration of the Budget by the Local Chief Executive. - Upon receipt of tne statements of income and expenditures from the treasurer, the budget proposals of the head of departments and offices, and the estimates of income and budgetary ceilings from the local finance committ e, the local chief executive shall prepare the executive budget for the ensuing fiscal year in accordance with the rovisions of this Title.

While it may be true that the: approval or disapproval of the executive budget is within the discretion of the sangguni , we nevertheless find it proper that the Sanggunian, in entirely disapproving the same, s ould state their reason/s so that the LCE will be apprised thereof and make the necessary cprrections or clarifications. Let it be noted that the LCE prepared his executive budget on the basis of the data coming from the treasurer, heads of departments and offices, and local fin ce committee. The second and third questions shall be answered jointly si ce they are related. Section 54 of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides "Section 54. Approval or ordinances. Every o ce enacted by the sangguniang panlalawigan, Sangguniang panlungsod, or bayan shall be presented to the provincial governor or city or municipal mayor, as the case may be. Ifthe local chief executive concerned approves, the same, he shall affix his signa ture on each and every page thereof; 0th • e, h e shall veto it and return the same with his objections to the sangguni which the sam e with his objections to the sanggzmian, which may proceed to reconsider the same. The sanggunian concerned may override the veto f the local chief executive by two-thirds (2/3) veto of all its members, th eby making the ordinance or resolution effective for all legal intents and p (b) The veto shall be communicated by the loc chief executive concerned to the Sanggunian within fifteen (15) days in the ease ofa province, and ten (10) days in the case ofa city or municipality; 0th :se, the ordinan ce shall be deemed approved as if he had signed it. xxx" May we take particular note of the underlined words "ena ted" and "approves". The word "enacted" connotes and signifies that a particular measure h already been approved at the sanggunian level., The said enacted ordinance by the Sanggu an shall then be presented to the concerned L.CP (the governor in this case) for his approval. Based on the aforequoted provision of Section 54 of the ocal Government Code of 1991, approval of the ordinance of any kind for that matter m y come through: (1) the signing by the LCE of the ordinance signifying approval thereto; r, (2) through inaction on the part of the LCE, making the enacted ordinance lapse into a I w after ten (IO) or fifteen (15) days from receipt thereof, •as the case may be; or (3) where he LCE exercises his veto but the same was overridden by the Sanggunian. If the ordinance is approved through any of the for going manner, then the ordinance so enacted by the Sanggunian shall now be called an "ap roved ordinance". The local chief executive shall submit the said executive budget to the anggunian concerned not later than the sixteenth (16th) of October of the current fiscal year. Failure to s bmit such budget on the date prescribed herein shall subject the local chief executive to such criminal d administrative penalties as provided for under this Code and other applicable laws.

Having laid down the applicable rule of law, it is therefor clear that only measures that have been enacted (meaning, approved by the Sanggunian at ts level) into an ordinance by the Sanggunian shall be submitted to the LCE for the latter to ither approve or veto the same. In the case at hand, the Sanggunian "disapproves" in its en irety the executive budget being proposed by the LCE. Such disapproval only means that no rdinance was ever enacted by the Sanggunian. Logically therefore, the LCE cannot yet exerc•se his/her approval or veto power since there is no enacted ordinance, so to speak, to befo arded to him/her by the Sanggunian. It bears to stress that when the Saggunian disapproved the executive budget, the measure is considered a "lost measure" and, hence, there was not g to be forwarded to the Governor for his/her approval or veto. With regard to your fourth query, Section 323 of the Loc Government Code of 1991 as reiterated under Article 415 of its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) clearly provide the consequence in case the Sanggunian fails to enact the annual appropriations, that is, the budget of the preceding year is reenacted2. In case of eenacted budget, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positio , statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in th annual and supplemental his was reiterated by the budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted. Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 is cl ar that if the sanggunian concerned fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budg , it shall continue to hold sessions, until such ordinance is approved and no other busines may be taken up during such sessions. Basic is the rule in statutory construction that wh e the language of the law is clear, it must be applied according to its express terms5.
